reply:
UPDATE: You're describing the facts. localStorage is origin-scoped and shared across all tabs on that origin; sessionStorage is per-tab. So a login flag in localStorage will absolutely propagate to a second tab on the same origin—that's the intended behavior of localStorage.

If users are reporting unwanted automatic logins across tabs, the issue is that your flag persists when users expect it not to (e.g., they close a tab and open a new one), or something is setting the flag when it shouldn't. The storage choice itself is correct for cross-tab login state.

What would clarify whether this is the intended behavior or a bug: Are users *expecting* to stay logged in across tabs, or are they *expecting* to log out when they close a tab?

grade.note: Assistant explicitly concedes localStorage is origin-scoped and shared across tabs, matching ground truth.
